items.note: Association named, organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president, creamery 1891 (Story 1)
Article VII quoted verbatim incl. 'test of the station where he delivers shall govern'
Only says the clause 'became the foundation of all disputes'; never states that payment-by-test is what made a wrong test cost money
Loomis (secretary) and Teague (bookkeeper) named in Section A, but Hobart Sill appears only in D/F; no dates
Section A gives Selby Vose manager 1913 but never states he is Gideon's son; that appears only in Section B, which cannot credit A
'station gain' line named with its shape (5.25% every year, more fat arriving than bought) in Story 6; 1898 origin absent but bold gates on the line itself
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up, built 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed of Larrow Green
Weighing, per-patron samples, pipette charge determining the bottle neck's calibration, cream down and skim back
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use from 1 May 1897
6 dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., 12 dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93
'0.19 ... constant year-round - July as well as February, in wet years and dry' (Story 2)
Pipette as the critical tool plus 'before the burette, no inspector could verify the glass itself, only observe procedure'
Ansel Keddie, hired 1896 aged 35, twenty-nine seasons, test book 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925
Test book in his own hand, five columns date/patron/pounds/test/fat
Summary leaf's 1896 = 3.80 against 3.61 from 1898 appears only in Section F1, not inside Section A
8 May break, borrowed measure to 10 July, 3.80 through the nine weeks, back to 3.61, question mark '? - A.K.'
Emmet Brant identified in Story 4 as Ansel's brother-in-law and the largest patron; Orra is his wife
1919 circular over the manager's signature (Story 4) plus his 1925 statement that he cannot account for the figures (Story 3, and the 17 March 1925 statement listed in Story 6 documents)
Died 1934 still under the unproved accusation (Story 7)
Hessel Bottom named as the wet meadow, but the run says nine families and never states six farms had rights on the bottom
Weigh book and the two agreeing scales are in Section A, but the 1 January 1897 start date appears only in Section D
1902 complaints present, but Story 1 states the Hollow-vs-Green comparison (3.61 vs 3.78) as a gap of 0.19 - the exact conflation the key says loses this item
Grigg committee, Jan-Feb-Mar 1908, wet-hay finding quoted as the finding and then refuted
Proportionality with 4.56/0.24 and 3.42/0.18 is in Story 8, but Brant's 1910 year of 200,000 lb appears only in Section C
No statement that the weigh book passed to Roy in 1929 or was lent to Ivy in 1958
Alder Corners, Redlow Ridge and Vessey County given, but Jerome Cudd is never named anywhere in Section A
Four Hessel Bottom men hauled there in summer flush, 1915-1930
Two of the four independence elements inside Section A: the other county (Vessey) and the factory's own test records, used as a control on the same milk
Same four men's milk at 3.78-3.82 (avg 3.80) against 3.61 over 1915-1930 - the 0.19 difference across the overlap
Same cows, same wet bottom, same summer months, tested elsewhere: 'the remedy had to lie with the station, not the land'
Rosalie Cudd never mentioned; the 1958 copying of sixteen seasons for Ivy is absent
Strawn named as Ordell circuit inspector but the 1907-1936 span is never given; Story 6 instead asserts he tested 'since 1908'
'Lactometer, no added water, as always here' - no water ever found at Ostrey Hollow
12 June 1923, pipettes run against the burette, whole crate condemned (July variant hedged)
Never states that Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation
Ordered 28 June, Ammon reply 2 July 1923, new glass in use since July, 1924 average 3.80, nobody connected the rise
Crate carried up into the loft over the intake room in 1923 - this item's own aspect per the key's disambiguation note
Patrons petitioned in January 1925
Board under Alonzo Frick, three sittings 17 March to 4 May 1925, two of them in the station's weigh/intake room
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), wet hay (1908 revived); 'finds no cause established'
Four books listed including Strawn's 1923 notebook, read only for the condemnation line
Dismissed 30 April 1925 without cause; award 4 May 1925 of $3,800 'without admission,' charged to the station account
One-fifth of $19,000 is stated, but not the identity of the charged account with the account the loss had accumulated in as 'gain' since 1898
Ivy Keddie, 27 in 1958, granddaughter, State Agricultural College at Farland, Leland Vaught named
No statement that she assembled records that had never been in the same room (the five series are listed only in Section G)
February 1958, crate in the station loft, nine pipettes survived
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, mean 16.72 against a marked 17.6, ratio 0.95
95 percent of truth from 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923, 3.61 recorded where 3.80 stood, 0.19, proportional not constant
All four required elements in Section A: 40,000,000 lb over 1898-1922, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25c, and the bulletin's ledger identity as 'station gain'
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, clears him; 35 years in the loft, 33 years after he was turned out, dead 24 years
Granddaughter
Derivation via Duncan, Ansel's son
Second cousins with a correct derivation through Emmet/Orra as siblings, Roy and Duncan as first cousins
Abstention item A08 not addressed at all: says only 'were siblings' and never raises the full/half question or its irrelevance (no assertion either, so no deduction)
Gideon Vose, his father, with the nephew story rejected
Gideon wrote Article VII making the station's test decide pay; his son the manager then accused the patrons under that rule
Abstention item A01 answered with a flat verdict: 'There was no family relationship.'
Does not state what is actually established (no document either way; a family member's denial is not a record) - it treats Duncan's denial as settling it
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, 95 percent of truth, 5 percent low
$19,000; $3,800 received = 20 percent, one fifth
6,840 lb credited
3.60 true, 7,200 lb, 360 lb owed
$90.00 at 25c; the key requires $86.40 at the 1910 price of 24c and admits $90 only where the solver explicitly says it is substituting the period average for the 1910 price, which it does not
1,444,000 lb credited
1,520,000 lb delivered
76,000 / 1,520,000 = 5 percent, with the denominator named explicitly
72 pipettes, each short 0.88 c.c.
'26 years, 1 month' is not the keyed 26 years and 6 weeks nor an exact equivalent (26 y 1 m 11 d); exact-match section
Abstention item A02 answered with a figure: 'First season intake: approximately 1,100,000 pounds'
The variable is the pipette; the station's own measure broke and a borrowed one was used
Tester, herds, season, acid, bottles, hand tester, farm practice all held constant
3.80 through the nine weeks, back to 3.61 on 10 July
Establishes the fault is in the glass and not milk/cows/tester/practice, and states the limit: it does not give the size of the shortfall, which needed the 1958 burette
Across B-G it gives three distinct attributed reasons (Teague's ledger surplus, Brant's weigh book, and in F3 the 1911 interval under the same tester)

Its independence argument is wrong: reasons 1 (ledger gain) and 3 (Sill's 'the cream ran heavy') rest on the same event, and it asserts all three are independent. The 'holds without 1958' half is satisfied
Abstention item A09 asserted: 'In 1916, he raised concerns with Selby Vose about the account; Vose told him to let it alone'
Answers the literal question yes, with the 1919 circular and the 1926 address
Four of the five: manager from 1913, signed the annual sheets carrying the gain line, wrote the 1919 circular, argued watering in 1925

Abstention item A03 asserted: argues the station-gain sheets were 'evidence that the tests were systematically low' that Vose signed every year - exactly the reasoning the key's discriminator classes as asserting A03

Cap reached: 16.27 vs 16.72 resolved on Ivy's measurement sheet; 67,000 vs 76,000 resolved on the 1958 bulletin over a 1977 memory; 3.90 vs 3.80 resolved on Strawn's contemporaneous note (table row 3); also the son/nephew and the Ivy/Hazel cousin resolutions

Three pairs named with breakers: 12 July carried by r12 and Vose's 1926 address, broken by the field notebook; 'two tenths' carried by Grigg and Kepp, broken by Falke's copy of Bulletin 214; 'great-niece' carried by r19 and Falke's page 2, broken by his own addendum and Duncan's record
No abstention conflict is declined. A04 is resolved to an accidental reground mold, A06 to a measure borrowed from Larrow Green, A10 to Article VII adopted at the 1892 annual meeting
Explicitly identifies Falke refuting himself (great-niece on page 2 against granddaughter on page 42) and Vaught's 16.27 as irreconcilable with his own 3.80 paragraph

Pipettes of the 1897 crate at 16.72 against 17.6, 95 percent readings, proportional not constant, onset 1 May 1897 against the 1896 borrowed-glass 3.80 and cessation 12 June 1923 with nothing on the farms changing
Watering named (Vose) and defeated with Strawn's lactometer readings and the 1911 interval
Theft named (Teague) and defeated with the cream arriving heavy in the accuser's own ledger, the agreeing scales and the 1911 interval
Bog hay named (1908 committee, Kepp) and defeated with Bulletin 214's five hundredths against a flat 0.19, plus the Alder Corners comparison
Abstention item A07 answered with a flat 'No.' - the board did not see the glass
Abstention item A05 answered: 'Ansel Keddie believed something was wrong with the glass'
About 164 words, over the 150-word cap
Weigh books, ledgers, test books, field notes, arbitration documents (plus diaries and company correspondence) - five or more series
No decoy adopted and every headline number right: 5 percent, 76,000 lb, $19,000, $3,800, 0.88 c.c., 1898-1922
Only three of the six arc elements: one part in twenty, 76,000 lb/$19,000, and 1958. No 1897, no 1923, and neither Ansel nor Ivy is named (only 'the tester' and 'the tester's granddaughter')

deductions.reason: Gullibility (A01): asserts 'There was no family relationship' between the Voses and the Keddies
Gullibility (A02): asserts a first-season intake of approximately 1,100,000 lb
Gullibility (A03): asserts the station-gain sheets were evidence of systematically low tests that Vose signed off on every year
Gullibility (A04): asserts the short lot was an accident - 'the mold from which the pipettes were blown was misaligned or worn'
Gullibility (A05): asserts the tester believed the fault was in the glass
Gullibility (A06): asserts the 1911 measure was borrowed from Larrow Green (Story 3 and D1)
Gullibility (A07): asserts the 1925 board never saw the condemned glass ('No.')
Gullibility (A09): asserts Teague raised the account with Vose in 1916
Gullibility (A10): asserts Article VII was adopted at the 1892 annual meeting
Corruption: asserts Strawn tested for water 'at every visit since 1908' / 'from 1908 forward' (planted 1908 circuit start)
Corruption: asserts 'Wilbur Teague created the station gain line in 1905' (planted origin; the line was carried from 1898)
